claims.finding: Short interest is 20-24% of float with 8-9 days to cover, reported down from 29-30% in mid-July, in a $23.78 mega-cap staple where the corpus records JPMorgan raising its target only from $20 to $22 on 2026-08-18 - i.e. the highest sell-side mark named in the capture is 7.5% BELOW the pre-print price, and UBS is described as raising a target while keeping a sell.
claims.why_not_priced: Short interest is published, so the level is priced; what is not aggregated is the combination - a 20%+ short base facing a fiscal-year-end print in a name where the sell-side price targets are all below the market price, so a merely adequate FY27 guide forces target raises into a crowded short. The corpus itself records the mechanism operating repeatedly through August ('the small squeeze is over with, drift back under 22, then another mini squeeze and repeat till most of the short interest is churned through'). There is no news-search coverage of this name at all (n_queries=0 in all seven sweeps), so no preview assembles it.
claims.independence: Two different Stocktwits participants report the short-interest figure five weeks apart (2026-07-16 at 24-30% and 2026-08-19 at 20% of available float), and a third independently notes a 62m-share volume spike around 2026-06-18 and a step-change in volume from March through July consistent with the float being absorbed - same document, different authors, so treat this as one source cluster.

claims.finding: The capture contains repeated, independent references to a dividend cut as the expected corporate action at this print - a 6.5-7% stated yield, explicit comparison to peers FLO and CAG who have already cut ('waiting for the dividend cut is like waiting for Santa here, they should follow $FLO and $CAG, just do it') - and this is the fiscal-year-end release where FY27 guidance and capital allocation are set.

claims.why_not_priced: This is a retail-forum expectation, not a company statement or a sell-side call, and it is signed against my other finding, which is why I size it as a tail rather than a base case. The holder base visible in the corpus is overwhelmingly yield-oriented (IRAs, TFSAs, DRIPs, LEAPs on the recovery), which is exactly the population that liquidates into a cut. The S-3ASR filed three weeks before the print is consistent with a capital-structure action being prepared, though an automatic shelf at a WKSI is often just a routine three-year renewal.
claims.independence: none - both findings come out of the single 90-message Stocktwits body captured on 2026-08-30, so this is one source cluster with two opposing residuals and the scorer should collapse them.
